propositions: A ticket directory with no CREATE or SNAPSHOT event exists in the store after a process death during the write window (makedirs -> stage temp -> atomic rename), persisting until manually removed.

The plan-relation reducer walks the store directory listing, encounters the event-less directory, and fails with reducer-error; this failure is surfaced as INDETERMINATE on unrelated tickets whose relation graphs the snapshot traverses.
The event-less directory is invisible to git (git cannot track empty directories) and never appears in git status, so it is undetectable via branch inspection and cannot be repaired by pulling.

The reducer was made tolerant of event-less directories by skipping them with a named warning instead of failing the entire snapshot; the writer continues creating directories before the first event to avoid unsafe concurrent cleanup races.

The writer-side cleanup approach is unsafe under the store's concurrency model (many sessions write one shared .tickets-tracker) and cannot repair existing broken clones, so only reader-side tolerance achieves full remediation.
